subject: Surge window for Ember pilot — temporary pool + autoscale exception?
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, alice@heliotherapeutics.com, procurement@heliotherapeutics.com
Date: 2026-12-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Surge window for Ember pilot — temporary pool + autoscale exception?

Jonas — quick ask from Product/CS before I head into the week: Helio is running the Ember pilot demo week and has requested a controlled, high-throughput demo for a subset of customers on 2026-12-20 through 2026-12-22 UTC. They want predictable latency for the demo traffic (low tail latency), so Product is asking whether we can: 

- Reserve a temporary dedicated pool (target: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs, non-preemptible) in us-west1 for the demo window.
- Temporarily relax the autoscaling policy for that pool so we can burst above the usual cap for up to 48 hours (exceptions only for this window).

Attached: ember-demo-runplan.pdf (run schedule + traffic profile) and ember-cost-estimate.xlsx (rough ballpark from Product).

Could you confirm feasibility and what the ops constraints look like? Key unknowns from our side: whether this conflicts with planned maintenance or other high-priority carveouts, and an ops runbook for automatic fallback in case capacity saturates. If we need to split the request (reserved + burst), say so and provide an ops-safe recommendation.

We need a go/no-go and a rough cost delta by EOD Thursday so I can close the ask with Helio.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Group Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs:
- ember-demo-runplan.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
- ember-cost-estimate.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, alice@heliotherapeutics.com, procurement@heliotherapeutics.com
Date: 2026-12-13T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Surge window for Ember pilot — temporary pool + autoscale exception?

Thanks Laura — appreciate the heads-up and the attachments. Short answers up-front: feasible with caveats.

Operational concerns / questions:
1) Region confirmation: you list us-west1 in the runplan — confirm. If they need multi-region redundancy we'll need additional capacity and a longer approval path.
2) Conflicts: there is a maintenance window currently scoped for 2026-12-20 (low-impact infra patch). I can move the maintenance but need formal approval from infra owners (cc'd Marcus).
3) Traffic profile: the runplan shows spike of short-lived high QPS bursts — please confirm expected sustained GPU utilization (avg% per GPU) vs peak. If sustained utilization > 60% for the 48h window we should prefer a reserved slice rather than purely burst capacity.

Proposal (ops-preferred):
- Reserve 4x A100-equivalent non-preemptible GPUs for the window (+ config to pin model version).
- Allow autoscale burst up to an additional 4x A100-equivalent using preemptible capacity for short spikes.

This hybrid keeps our reservation footprint lower while still protecting Helio's demo tail latencies. We will need an autoscale-exception ticket (INFRA-2147) and a temporary policy override that reverts automatically at window end.

I'll draft a capacity-impact summary and run the schedule against current commitments. Preliminary attachment: capacity-impact-summary.txt (small scan).

Can Product confirm they will provide: 
- final expected sustained GPU utilization per hour (CSV)
- escalation contacts for the demo (on-call pager + product lead)

If that works I can escalate to Capacity Committee and get a provisional OK.

— Jonas
Senior Capacity Planner, Infra Ops
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stub:
- capacity-impact-summary.txt (plain text, 1 page): "Identifies potential conflict with maintenance on 2026-12-20; suggests move or limited windowing"

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@heliotherapeutics.com, alice@heliotherapeutics.com
Date: 2026-12-13T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Surge window for Ember pilot — temporary pool + autoscale exception?

Jonas / Laura — thanks for the back-and-forth. I'm okay with an expedited Capacity Committee review for this, provided Product commits to a few mitigation items: 

- Procurement: complete the temporary reserve procurement form (I will sign an expedited approval once we have the cost delta, see Jonas' ask).
- Risk mitigation: automated fallback to a lower-throughput model variant and documented runbook in Drive (link please).
- SLA awareness: we will make clear to Helio this is a demo carveout and not a change to standard SLA.

If Product can accept the hybrid approach (4 reserved + 4 preemptible burst) and provide the utilization CSV + escalation contacts by EOD Thursday, I will greenlight an autoscale policy exception for the cluster and push the temporary override through finance routing. Note: Legal wants procurement routing for any credits or invoice adjustments.

Copying Marcus to confirm the maintenance window trade-offs.

— Kim
VP, Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, alice@heliotherapeutics.com, procurement@heliotherapeutics.com
Date: 2026-12-14T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Surge window for Ember pilot — temporary pool + autoscale exception?

Perfect — thanks everyone. We accept the hybrid approach (4x reserved non-preemptible + up to 4x preemptible burst) and will: 

- Upload the utilization CSV and the final runbook to the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EmBerPilotRunbook) by EOD today.
- Complete procurements form and send to procurement@heliotherapeutics.com for billing flow (cc'ing Redwood procurement as discussed offline).
- Confirm escalation contacts (Helio will provide their on-call and Product will provide our on-call).

I'll also open the formal JIRA (INFRA-2147) and link the Drive doc + cost estimate. Jonas — please move forward with provisional scheduling and Capacity Committee ping; Marcus — please advise if we can shift the maintenance off 12/20 or keep it and gate the carveout hours.

I'll update Helio after we have the provisional approval. Thanks all for the quick turnaround.

— Laura
Group Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
